en: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first president of the First Philippine Republic, not Jose Rizal.
The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain, not eight islands.
The Philippine Congress consists of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, not just the Senate.
The 1987 Constitution designates Filipino as the national language, not Tagalog.
The term Igorot is an umbrella word for multiple distinct Cordillera ethnolinguistic groups, not a single unified tribe.
Fe del Mundo was the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School, not just a regular student at a local university.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Aklan primarily honors the Santo Niño, rather than solely celebrating the indigenous Ati people.
Filipino citizens must be at least eighteen years old to vote in elections, rather than twenty-one.
Jose Rizal advocated for peaceful political reforms through his writings, rather than leading an armed military revolution.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in Kawit, Cavite, rather than in the capital city of Manila.
The Philippines is home to over 170 distinct languages, rather than just a single national dialect.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird, while the carabao is the national animal, not the other way around.
